sentences.en: There was once a man who had an Ass and a Lap-dog.
sentences.zh: 从前有个人，养着一头驴和一只哈巴狗。

sentences.en: The Ass was housed in the stable with plenty of oats and hay to eat and was as well off as an ass could be.
sentences.zh: 驴住在马厩里，有充足的燕麦和干草吃，日子过得再舒坦不过。

sentences.en: The little Dog was made a great pet of by his master, who fondled him and often let him lie in his lap …
sentences.zh: 那只小狗却被主人当成宝贝，主人爱抚它，常让它卧在膝上……

sentences.en: … and if he went out to dinner, he would bring back a tit-bit or two to give him when he ran to meet him on his return.
sentences.zh: ……主人外出赴宴，回来时小狗跑去迎接，他总会带回一两口好吃的东西给它。

sentences.en: The Ass had, it is true, a good deal of work to do, carting or grinding the corn, or carrying the burdens of the farm …
sentences.zh: 驴确实有不少活要干：拉车、磨谷，或者驮运农场的重物……

sentences.en: … and ere long he became very jealous, contrasting his own life of labour with the ease and idleness of the Lap-dog.
sentences.zh: ……不久它就十分嫉妒起来，拿自己劳苦的日子对比哈巴狗的安逸闲散。

sentences.en: At last one day he broke his halter, and frisking into the house just as his master sat down to dinner, he pranced and capered about …
sentences.zh: 终于有一天它挣断了缰绳，正当主人坐下吃饭时欢跳着冲进屋里，蹦来跳去……

sentences.en: … mimicking the frolics of the little favourite, upsetting the table and smashing the crockery with his clumsy efforts.
sentences.zh: ……模仿那小宠物的嬉闹，笨手笨脚地撞翻了桌子，把碗碟砸得粉碎。

sentences.en: Not content with that, he even tried to jump on his master's lap, as he had so often seen the dog allowed to do.
sentences.zh: 它还不满足，甚至想跳到主人膝上去——它常看见狗被允许这样。

sentences.en: At that the servants, seeing the danger their master was in, belaboured the silly Ass with sticks and cudgels …
sentences.zh: 这时仆人们见主人有危险，便用棍棒狠打这头蠢驴……

sentences.en: … and drove him back to his stable half dead with his beating.
sentences.zh: ……把它打得半死，赶回了马厩。

sentences.en: "Alas!" he cried, "all this I have brought on myself.
sentences.zh: 「唉！」它叫道，「这都是我自找的。

sentences.en: Why could I not be satisfied with my natural and honourable position, without wishing to imitate the ridiculous antics of that useless …
sentences.zh: 我为什么不安守自己本分而体面的位置，偏要去学那没用的……

sentences.en: … little Lap-dog?"
sentences.zh: 「……小哈巴狗的滑稽把戏呢？」

title: The Shepherd's Boy and the Wolf
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Shepherd's Boy was tending his flock near a village …
sentences.zh: 一个牧童在村子附近放羊……

sentences.en: … and thought it would be great fun to hoax the villagers by pretending that a Wolf was attacking the sheep …
sentences.zh: ……他觉得假装有狼来袭击羊群、骗骗村里人一定很好玩……

sentences.en: … so he shouted out, "Wolf! wolf!" and when the people came running up he laughed at them for their pains.
sentences.zh: ……于是大喊「狼来了！狼来了！」等人们跑来，他又笑人家白忙一场。

sentences.en: He did this more than once, and every time the villagers found they had been hoaxed, for there was no Wolf at all.
sentences.zh: 他这样干了好几次，每次村民都发现自己被骗了，根本没有狼。

sentences.en: At last a Wolf really did come, and the Boy cried, "Wolf! wolf!" as loud as he could …
sentences.zh: 后来狼真的来了，牧童拼命大喊「狼来了！狼来了！」……

sentences.en: … but the people were so used to hearing him call that they took no notice of his cries for help.
sentences.zh: ……可人们听惯了他的喊叫，对他的求救毫不理会。

sentences.en: And so the Wolf had it all his own way, and killed off sheep after sheep at his leisure.
sentences.zh: 于是狼为所欲为，不慌不忙地把羊一只只咬死。

sentences.en: You cannot believe a liar even when he tells the truth.
sentences.zh: 爱说谎的人，即使说真话也没人信。

sentences.en: A Queen Bee from Hymettus flew up to Olympus with some fresh honey from the hive as a present to Jupiter …
sentences.zh: 一只来自许墨托斯的蜂后飞到奥林匹斯山，带着蜂巢里新鲜的蜜献给朱庇特……

sentences.en: … who was so pleased with the gift that he promised to give her anything she liked to ask for.
sentences.zh: ……朱庇特很喜欢这份礼物，便答应给她任何她想要的东西。

sentences.en: She said she would be very grateful if he would give stings to the bees, to kill people who robbed them of their honey.
sentences.zh: 她说，若他赐给蜜蜂毒刺，好刺死那些偷蜜的人，她将感激不尽。

sentences.en: Jupiter was greatly displeased with this request, for he loved mankind …
sentences.zh: 朱庇特对这个请求很不高兴，因为他爱护人类……

sentences.en: … but he had given his word, so he said that stings they should have.
sentences.zh: ……但他已许下诺言，便说既如此就赐它们刺。

sentences.en: The stings he gave them, however, were of such a kind that whenever a bee stings a man the sting is left in the wound and the bee dies.
sentences.zh: 然而他给的刺是这样的：蜂一刺人，刺便留在伤口里，而蜂自己也会死去。

sentences.en: Evil wishes, like fowls, come home to roost.
sentences.zh: 恶愿如鸡，终归自家栖处。

sentences.en: A Pedlar who owned an Ass one day bought a quantity of salt, and loaded up his beast with as much as he could bear.
sentences.zh: 一个货郎有一头驴。有一天他买了一批盐，把驴装得能驮多少就驮多少。

sentences.en: On the way home the Ass stumbled as he was crossing a stream and fell into the water.
sentences.zh: 回家路上，驴过小溪时失足跌进了水里。

sentences.en: The salt got thoroughly wetted and much of it melted and drained away …
sentences.zh: 盐全湿透了，大半化掉流走了……

sentences.en: … so that, when he got on his legs again, the Ass found his load had become much less heavy.
sentences.zh: ……所以当驴重新站起来时，发现担子轻了许多。

sentences.en: His master, however, drove him back to town and bought more salt, which he added to what remained in the panniers, and started out again.
sentences.zh: 可是主人把它赶回城里，又买了些盐，加到驮筐里剩下的那部分上，重新出发。

sentences.en: No sooner had they reached a stream than the Ass lay down in it, and rose, as before, with a much lighter load.
sentences.zh: 一到溪边，驴就趴进水里，像上次一样轻了许多地站起来。

sentences.en: But his master detected the trick, and turning back once more, bought a large number of sponges, and piled them on the back of the Ass.
sentences.zh: 可主人看穿了这个把戏，又折回去买了一大堆海绵，堆在驴背上。

sentences.en: When they came to the stream the Ass again lay down …
sentences.zh: 到了溪边，驴又趴了下去……

sentences.en: … but this time, as the sponges soaked up large quantities of water, he found …
sentences.zh: ……可这一次，海绵吸足了水，它发现……

sentences.en: … when he got up on his legs, that he had a bigger burden to carry than ever.
sentences.zh: ……站起来时，背上的担子比先前更重了。

sentences.en: You may play a good card once too often.
sentences.zh: 好牌也有打滥的时候。
